fixes.explanation: True, baker. Joseph takes the body and wraps it in a clean linen cloth (Matthew 27:59). The text gives us that detail right there, clean linen. I think that says Joseph handled the body with care.
It's actually true, friend. The text says Joseph took the body and wrapped it in a clean linen cloth (Matthew 27:59). Clean is the word the text uses. I think Joseph was careful about it.
Right, baker, it's Joseph's own new tomb, the one cut into the rock (Matthew 27:60). Think about that. A rich man lays Jesus' body in a new tomb that's his own. I think that says a lot about Joseph.

Not a cart, baker. Imagine a cart parked at the entrance with a sticky note on it: "Back in five minutes." The text says Joseph rolled a great stone across the entrance and went away (Matthew 27:60). A stone, not a cart.

Right, baker. The chief priests and Pharisees say, "we remember that while He was alive that deceiver said, ‘After three days I will rise again.’" (Matthew 27:63) They call Him a deceiver, but they remember His words. That's what they bring to Pilate.

Not this one, friend. Those words were said by others, who said, "…let Him come down now from the cross…" (Matthew 27:42). What the priests and Pharisees remember is, "After three days I will rise again." (Matthew 27:63)

Not that, baker. Elijah comes up when someone near the cross says, "Let us see if Elijah comes to save Him." (Matthew 27:49) That's what that person said, not what the priests and Pharisees remember. They remember Jesus saying, "After three days I will rise again." (Matthew 27:63)
